Subject: Foundry pilot -- converting faucet to committed allowance?

Hi Soojin,

Thanks again for the demo last week. Foundry's accelerator cohort is excited about the throughput we saw. Two asks from our finance lead: 1) can the provisional "faucet" allowance from the pilot be converted into a committed monthly allowance (so we can forecast spend), and 2) if converted, what does the billing path look like (monthly invoice vs applied promo credit)?

We'd also like visibility on whether conversion changes the promo discount floor you shared. Attached is a very short SOW that shows the cohort size. Can we get a quick note on options by EOD Wednesday?

Thanks,
Aisha
Foundry Labs — Program Lead
attachments: sow-provisional-faucet-draft.pdf (pdf, 120KB)

From: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.com>

Date: Mon, 3 May 2027 11:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Foundry pilot -- converting faucet to committed allowance?

Hi Aisha —

Appreciate the clear ask. Short answer: yes, we can convert the provisional faucet into a committed monthly allowance, and there are two billing patterns we typically use:

- Promo-anchored invoice: we issue monthly invoices for the committed amount and apply a promo/credit ledger line (keeps accounting clean for cohorts).
- Commitment conversion with seat-topup: convert faucet to an advance credit (one-time prepaid invoice) that burns down monthly; this is preferred when sponsors want a single PO.

Converting does change discounting thresholds slightly — larger committed tranches unlock incremental sponsor discounts. I attached a pricing workbook with three tranche examples so you can see the math.

Quick ask for you: can you confirm whether the sponsor will accept monthly invoices or needs a single PO prepay? If PO/prepay, we'll route to finance for an SLA addendum.

I'll loop Ben and Lauren for the recommended path and any commercial flex.

Best,
Soojin
Senior Account Executive, Redwood Inference

On Tue, May 4, 2027 at 9:03 AM Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.com> wrote:
> Appreciate the clear ask. Short answer: yes, we can convert the provisional faucet into a committed monthly allowance...

Adding context from commercial: if Foundry moves to a 6-month committed tranche (recommended for predictable throughput), we can offer a 10% cohort discount and an onboarding credit equivalent to one month of estimated consumption. If they want the sponsor to keep the ledger separate (sponsorship routing), we can do a dual-invoice path: Redwood invoices Foundry; sponsor reimburses via predetermined invoices.

Caveat: any committed discount requires a written addendum to avoid retroactive adjustments. Lauren — can you prepare a one-paragraph addendum template we can send to Foundry?

Ben
Director, Partnerships Ops
Redwood Inference

From: Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.com>

Date: Wed, 5 May 2027 10:12:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Foundry pilot -- converting faucet to committed allowance?

Aisha —

Draft addendum attached (see summary below). Key points:
- Commitment term: 6 months; monthly committed allowance: defined in SOW appendix A.
- Billing: monthly invoice with promo credit applied (or single prepay PO if sponsor requests).
- Discount: 10% on committed consumption; onboarding credit equals 1-month estimated usage applied on first invoice.
- Termination: 30-day notice; unused prepaid credits do not roll beyond contract unless agreed.

If sponsor needs a single PO, finance will require the prepay invoice to include the sponsor legal name and billing contact. Aisha — can you confirm the sponsor legal entity and whether they'll accept monthly invoicing?

Attachment: redwood_foundry_addendum_draft.docx (docx, 12KB)

Thanks,
Lauren
Head of Commercial Contracts
